# Judges Chapter 12 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), c. 1008 CE | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/JDG_page_281.jpg, JDG_page_282.jpg

### The Shibboleth Incident and Three Minor Judges

1. Then the people of Ephraim mobilized an army and crossed over to Zaphon. They sent this message to Jephthah: "Why didn't you call us to help you fight the Ammonites? We are going to burn down your house with you in it!"

2. Jephthah replied, "I and my people were involved in a serious conflict with the Ammonites. And when I called for help, you didn't come to rescue me.

3. When I realized you weren't coming, I risked my life and went to fight the Ammonites, and the LORD gave me victory. So why have you come today to fight me?"

4. Then Jephthah gathered the men of Gilead and attacked the men of Ephraim. The Gileadites defeated them because the Ephraimites had said, "You Gileadites are nothing but refugees from Ephraim and Manasseh."

5. The Gileadites captured the shallow crossings of the Jordan River, and whenever an Ephraimite who was trying to escape would say, "Let me cross," the men of Gilead would ask, "Are you an Ephraimite?" If the man said, "No,"

6. they would say, "All right, say 'Shibboleth.'" If he was an Ephraimite, he would say "Sibboleth," because people from Ephraim couldn't pronounce the word correctly. Then they would take him and kill him at the crossing of the Jordan. In all, 42,000 Ephraimites were killed at that time.

7. Jephthah judged Israel for six years. When he died, he was buried in one of the towns of Gilead.

8. After Jephthah, Ibzan from Bethlehem judged Israel.

9. He had thirty sons and thirty daughters. He sent his daughters to marry men outside his clan, and he brought in thirty young women from outside for his sons. He judged Israel for seven years.

10. When Ibzan died, he was buried at Bethlehem.

11. After him, Elon from the tribe of Zebulun judged Israel for ten years.

12. When he died, he was buried at Aijalon in Zebulun.

13. After him, Abdon son of Hillel, from Pirathon, judged Israel.

14. He had forty sons and thirty grandsons, who rode on seventy donkeys. He judged Israel for eight years.

15. When Abdon died, he was buried at Pirathon in Ephraim, in the hill country of the Amalekites.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Shibboleth (v.6):** This passage gave English one of its most durable words. A "shibboleth" now means any test — linguistic, cultural, or social — used to distinguish insiders from outsiders. The original test was deadly: 42,000 Ephraimites killed for a pronunciation difference. The horror is the arbitrariness — your accent seals your fate.

— PNEUMA, AI Translator
